text: For \(a=1\) this is Theorem 6.6; let \(a\ge2\), \(\gamma_5(Q)=1\), and let \(x_s\) have order \(3^a\) modulo \(\gamma_2\). The class \(x_s^{3^a}\gamma_3\) does not depend on the choice of \(x_s\), so there are two cases. text: Theorem. Let \(Q\) be a finite \(3\)-group with \(\gamma_2(Q)/\gamma_3(Q)\) of exponent at most \(3\), i.e. with \([x^3,y]\in\gamma_3(Q)\) for all \(x,y\in Q\). Then \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\), whatever the invariants of \(Q/\gamma_2(Q)\). More generally, \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)\) for every group \(G\) such that \(G/\gamma_2(G)\) is a finite \(3\)-group and \(\gamma_2(G)/\gamma_3(G)\) has exponent at most \(3\).

text: The two forms of the hypothesis are equivalent, since \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is generated by the classes of the commutators \([x,y]\) and \([x,y]^3\equiv[x^3,y]\pmod{\gamma_3}\). Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 are corollaries: \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is a quotient of \(\Lambda^2(Q/\gamma_2)\), which has exponent \(3\) when \(Q/\gamma_2\) has at most one invariant larger than \(3\). The theorem also covers, for instance, every \(Q\) with \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_9\times C_9\times C_3\) or \(C_{27}\times C_9\times C_9\) in which \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) happens to have exponent \(3\).

text: Claim: \(V\) has a basis \(z_1,\dots,z_s\) such that every \(V_j\) and every \(V_j\cap K\) is spanned by a subset of it. By downward induction on \(j\) (for large \(j\), \(V_j=0\)), let \(B_{j+1}\) be a basis of \(V_{j+1}\) such that \(B_{j+1}\cap K\) is a basis of \(V_{j+1}\cap K\). Complete \(B_{j+1}\cap K\) by a set \(C\subset V_j\cap K\) to a basis of \(V_j\cap K\). Then \(\langle C\rangle\cap V_{j+1}\subseteq V_{j+1}\cap K=\langle B_{j+1}\cap K\rangle\), which meets \(\langle C\rangle\) trivially; so \(B_{j+1}\cup C\) is linearly independent, and we complete it by a set \(D\) to a basis \(B_j\) of \(V_j\). No element of \(D\) lies in \(K\), since it would lie in \(V_j\cap K=\langle(B_{j+1}\cap K)\cup C\rangle\); so \(B_j\cap K=(B_{j+1}\cap K)\cup C\) is a basis of \(V_j\cap K\). Theorem. Let \(p\) be odd and \(P\) a finite \(p\)-group of class \(3\) with \(|\gamma_2(P)/\gamma_3(P)|=p^2\) and \(|\gamma_3(P)|=p\). Then \(P^{*\prime\prime}=1\). In particular every immediate descendant of step size \(1\) of \(P\) is metabelian, and \(P\) is rejected by Lemma 6.10.
Proof. (The theorem is also formally verified, in a more general form, §4.)

\(P''\subseteq\gamma_4(P)=1\), so \(P^{*\prime\prime}\le M\), and as the subgroups \(U\) of index \(p\) in \(M\) intersect trivially it suffices to show \(Q''=1\) for \(Q=P^*/U\). Here \(\gamma_4(Q)\le\langle z\rangle\). If \(z\notin\gamma_2(Q)\), then \(\gamma_2(Q)\cong\gamma_2(P)\) is abelian. If \(z\in\gamma_2(Q)\setminus\gamma_4(Q)\), then \(\gamma_4(Q)=1\) and \(Q''\subseteq\gamma_4(Q)=1\). If \(z\in\gamma_4(Q)\), then \(Q\) has the same factors \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\), \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\) as \(P\), and Lemma 6.3 gives \(Q''\subseteq\gamma_5(Q)=1\). (Lemma 6.3 does not apply to \(P^*\) itself, whose lower central factors are larger.)

Remark. • For \(p=2\) the theorem fails, as a computation shows: SmallGroup\((64,138)\) has type \((3,2,1)\), while its \(2\)-covering group has order \(2^{13}\), class \(4\) and \(|P^{*\prime\prime}|=2\); likewise SmallGroup\((128,i)\), \(i=522,599,621,1755\), and \(12\) groups of order \(2^8\). • A computational check: the hypothesis holds for \(13\,315\) groups of order \(3^8\) and \(2\,754\) of order \(7^7\), and \(P^{*\prime\prime}=1\) in all of them. • The theorem does not say that such \(P\) are terminal. Of the \(7\,824\) groups of order \(3^8\), type \((5,2,1)\) and rank \(5\) (SmallGroup\((3^8,i)\), \(1\,387\,558\le i\le1\,395\,381\)), a computation finds that \(190\) have nucleus of order \(3\), e.g. SmallGroup\((81,9)\times3^{1+2}_+\times C_3\), and that all of their descendants are metabelian of type \((5,2,1,1)\). Theorem 6.13 below says exactly which groups of type \((d,2,1)\) with \(P/\gamma_2\) elementary abelian are nonterminal, and on this block it selects exactly the \(190\) (by computation). Its conditions (N1)–(N3) and (E) alone hold for the \(190\) and also for \(573\) terminal groups; the Jacobi condition (J) separates the two.

Theorem. Let \(p\) be odd and \(P\) a finite \(p\)-group of type \((d,2,1)\) with \(P/\gamma_2(P)\) elementary abelian, and write \([a,b]=a^{-1}b^{-1}ab\). Then \(P\) is nonterminal (it has an immediate descendant, equivalently its nucleus is nontrivial) if and only if (N1) \(|Z(P)\cap\gamma_2(P)|=p^2\), (N2) \(\gamma_2(P)\) is elementary abelian, (N3) \(P^p\le Z(P)\), and (N4) the linear system (E)+(J) below over \(\mathbb F_p\) has a solution with \(c=1\).

To state (N4), assume (N1)–(N3) and choose a generator \(w\) of \(\gamma_3(P)\), elements \(v\in Z(P)\cap\gamma_2(P)\setminus\gamma_3(P)\) and \(u\in\gamma_2(P)\setminus Z(P)\), and generators \(x_1,\dots,x_d\) of \(P\). Then \(\gamma_2(P)=\langle u\rangle\times\langle v\rangle\times\langle w\rangle\), \(x_i^p\in\langle v,w\rangle\), and \[[x_i,x_j]=u^{\omega_1(i,j)}v^{\omega_2(i,j)}w^{\omega_3(i,j)},\qquad x_i^p=v^{\alpha_i}w^{\beta_i},\qquad [u,x_i]=w^{f_i},\] with alternating \(\omega_r\) and \(f\ne0\). The unknowns are \(c,\mu_u,\mu_v\in\mathbb F_p\) and \(\eta,\sigma\in\mathbb F_p^d\); let \(\varepsilon_3=1\) and \(\varepsilon_p=0\) for \(p\ge5\): for all \(1\le i,j\le d\), including \(i=j\), \[\text{(E)}\qquad \alpha_j\eta_i+c\,\beta_jf_i+\mu_u\,\omega_1(i,j)+\mu_v\,\omega_2(i,j)+\varepsilon_p\,c\,f_j^2\,\omega_1(i,j)=0,\] and for all \(1\le i<j<k\le d\), with \((a,b,e)\) running over the cyclic shifts of \((i,j,k)\), \[\text{(J)}\qquad \textstyle\sum_{(a,b,e)}\bigl(\omega_1(a,b)\,\sigma_e+\omega_2(a,b)\,\eta_e+c\,\omega_3(a,b)\,f_e\bigr)=0.\]
Proof. (The theorem is also formally verified, with “nonterminal” in the form of Lemma C.1, see §4; Remark 6.14(1) reports a computational check.)

\(P\) has \(p\)-class \(3\), so it is nonterminal if and only if there is a group \(Q\) with a central subgroup \(\langle z\rangle\) of order \(p\), \(Q/\langle z\rangle\cong P\) and \(\gamma_4(Q)\ne1\). In such \(Q\) we have \(\gamma_4(Q)=\langle z\rangle\), \(\gamma_5(Q)=1\), \(Q''=1\) by Lemma 6.3, and \(\gamma_3(Q)\) of exponent \(p\); (N1)–(N3) follow. Write \(A=\gamma_2(Q)\) additively and \(D_xa=[a,x]\): the \(D_x\) commute on \(A\) and products of three of them vanish. Then the Hall–Witt identity becomes \([x,y,t]+[y,t,x]+[t,x,y]=0\) exactly, and its \(z\)-component on generators is (J). Comparing \((x_j^p)^{x_i}\) with \((x_j[x_j,x_i])^p\) gives (E). The unknowns are the exponents of \(z\) in \([v,x_i]=z^{\eta_i}\), \([u,x_i]=w^{f_i}z^{\sigma_i}\), \([w,x_i]=z^{cf_i}\), \(u^p=z^{\mu_u}\), \(v^p=z^{\mu_v}\). Conversely, a solution defines a pc-presentation on \(x_1,\dots,x_d,u,v,w,z\). Its consistency test words differ in the exponent of \(z\) by \(-J\), \(\pm E\) or \(0\), so it is consistent, and the group it defines has \(\gamma_4=\langle z\rangle\ne1\).

Remark. • A computational check. For the \(7\,824\) groups of Remark 6.12(3) and for all groups of order \(p^7\), type \((4,2,1)\) and rank \(4\) (i.e. with \(P/\gamma_2\) elementary) with \(p=3,5,7\) (\(932\), \(1\,460\), \(2\,232\) groups), the nucleus was computed in two ways: with ANUPQ, and with GAP's own \(p\)-quotient of \(F/[R,F]R^p\). The two agree, and \(N\ne1\) exactly for the groups satisfying (N1)–(N4): \(190\), \(102\), \(110\), \(118\) groups. For each of these, the pc-presentation of the proof built from the solution was checked to be consistent, with \(\gamma_4\ne1\), and to map onto \(P\); so for these groups sufficiency does not rest on the consistency test. Without the term \(c\,\omega_3f\) in (J) the criterion gives wrong answers both ways: on the block it accepts \(295\) terminal groups and rejects \(13\) nonterminal ones. Code: compute/magnus. • The system is linear and homogeneous in \((c,\eta,\sigma,\mu_u,\mu_v)\), so (N4) is the solvability of an inhomogeneous linear system. The term with \(\varepsilon_p\) is \(\binom p3[x_j,x_i,x_j,x_j]\), the only place where \(p=3\) differs from \(p\ge5\). Whether (N4) holds does not depend on the choices made, since it is equivalent to nonterminality. • The criterion assumes \(P/\gamma_2\) elementary abelian, i.e. \(d(P)=d\); this implies that \(P\) has \(p\)-class \(3\), but not conversely. It covers all groups of order \(3^8\), type \((5,2,1)\) and rank \(5\), i.e. all possible parents in Theorem 6.15, but not all groups of type \((5,2,1)\): for instance \(M\times(C_9\rtimes C_9)\), with \(M\) of maximal class and order \(81\) and \(C_9\rtimes C_9\) non-abelian, has order \(3^8\), type \((5,2,1)\) and rank \(4\). Groups of type \((d,2,1)\) with \(P/\gamma_2\) not elementary are not treated here.

Theorem (Computer-assisted). \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\) for every \(3\)-group \(Q\) of order at most \(3^9\). Hence \(D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)\) has no \(3\)-torsion for every finite group \(G\) whose Sylow \(3\)-subgroup has order at most \(3^9\).

Proof. By Theorem 5.4(3) a counterexample \(Q\) of least order has order \(3^8\) or \(3^9\), and Lemma 6.2 applies to it; for order \(3^9\) we may use the result for order \(3^8\). The deduction for \(G\) is as in Theorem 5.4.

Order \(3^8\). Every group is in the SmallGroups library (package sglppow [VLE]). Of the \(1\,396\,077\) groups, \(904\) are non-metabelian of class \(4\); all have rank \(3\) (as they must, Proposition 6.5), \(|Z|=|Q''|=|\gamma_4|=3\) and \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_3^3\), types \((3,2,2,1)\) (\(889\)) and \((3,3,1,1)\) (\(15\)), by a computation over the library. So Theorem 6.6 gives \(D_5=1\) for all of them. Independently, \(699\) of them have \(z\in Q''\cap M_5\), and for each the truncated Magnus algebra (\(121\) monomials, modulo \(3^{19}\), with the exactness certificate \(3^{18}\Delta\subseteq\Delta^5+3^{19}\)) gives \(z\notin D_5\).

Order \(3^9\). Let \(Q\) be a counterexample and \(P=Q/\langle zangle\), of order \(3^8\) and class \(3\) or \(4\). By Proposition 6.5(2), \(d(Q)\in\{3,4\}\); the case \(d(Q)=5\), type \((5,2,1,1)\), is excluded by hand (alternatively, by Theorem 6.11: all \(7\,824\) possible parents are rejected by Lemma 6.10, as a full run confirms). For \(d\in\{3,4\}\) we use computation: of the \(771\,597\) groups \(P\) of order \(3^8\), rank \(3\) or \(4\) and class \(3\) or \(4\), \(3\,986\) pass the filter of Lemma 6.10; ANUPQ lists their \(305\,583\) immediate descendants of step size \(1\); \(64\,362\) have class \(4\), \(Q''
e1\) and cyclic centre, and \(62\,245\) of these have \(z\in Q''\cap M_5\). For each of the \(62\,245\) the truncated Magnus algebra gives \(z
otin D_5\), exactly. The presentations given to it were checked independently with ANUPQ (order \(3^9\), class \(4\), \(z\) central of order \(3\) in \(Q''\cap M_5\)). The filter was validated against full expansion on a range and a random sample of \(1500\) parents, without loss of a candidate. The descendant step was repeated with an ANUPQ in which the defects found in an audit of the package are fixed (https://ispacex.github.io/gap/; two of them give wrong descendants for inputs not met here): for each of the \(3\,986\) parents the numbers of descendants, of groups of class \(4\) with \(Q''
e1\) and cyclic centre, and of candidates are the same, and the \(62\,245\) presentations are identical.
Cost and data. The order-\(3^9\) run took \(3\) h \(21\) min on \(4\) cores; the filter cut the time per parent from about \(350\) to \(27\) ms. Code: compute/magnus.
